그것.e: 그 (that) + 것 (thing); in speech usually 그거.

축하하다.forms: 축하해요 · 축하했어요 · 축하할 거예요 · 축하해 주세요

아침밥.x: I was busy, so I couldn't eat breakfast today.
아침밥.e: 아침 'morning' + 밥 'rice, meal'; in casual speech, 아침 alone also means breakfast.

정보.x: I found a lot of travel information online.

적금.ex: 저는 매달 10만 원씩 적금을 넣고 있어요.
적금.x: I'm putting 100,000 won into a savings plan every month.
적금.e: Literally 'piled-up money' — you add to it every month.
적금.t: Koreans say 적금을 붓다 or 적금을 넣다 for making the monthly deposits.

국민.m: the people (of a nation), citizens, nationals
국민.x: The president must work for the people.
국민.t: Pronounced [궁민] — nasalization: ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㅁ.

학점.ex: 이번 학기에 학점을 잘 받아서 기분이 좋아요.
학점.x: I'm happy because I got good grades this semester.
학점.t: Pronounced [학쩜]; it means both course credits (3학점) and your overall grades.

촌스럽다.ex: 이 디자인은 좀 촌스러운 것 같아요.
촌스럽다.x: I think this design is a bit tacky.

세뱃돈.m: New Year's money (given to children after a bow)
세뱃돈.x: On Lunar New Year, I bowed to my grandmother and received New Year's money.
세뱃돈.e: 세배 'New Year's bow' + 돈 'money'; the ㅅ links the two words.
세뱃돈.t: Pronounced [세배똔/세밷똔]; children bow first, then elders hand out the money.

소용없다.ex: 이미 끝난 일이라서 지금 후회해도 소용없어요.
소용없다.x: It's already over, so there's no use regretting it now.
소용없다.e: 소용 'use' + 없다 'not exist' — literally 'there's no use'.
소용없다.t: Pronounced [소용업따]; common pattern -아/어 봤자 소용없다 'it's no use even if you try.'

친환경.ex: 요즘은 친환경 제품을 사는 사람이 많아요.
친환경.x: These days a lot of people buy eco-friendly products.

마스크 팩.ex: 피곤한 날에는 마스크 팩을 붙이고 쉬어요.
마스크 팩.x: On tiring days, I put on a sheet mask and relax.
마스크 팩.e: Konglish from English 'mask' + 'pack'; English speakers say 'sheet mask'.
마스크 팩.t: Often just 팩; put one on is 팩을 하다/붙이다. Don't confuse with 마스크 alone, which usually means a face covering.

예술성.ex: 이 영화는 재미와 예술성을 모두 갖추었어요.
예술성.x: This movie has both entertainment value and artistic quality.

평론.ex: 그는 신문에 영화 평론을 쓰고 있어요.
평론.x: He writes film reviews for a newspaper.
평론.t: Pronounced [평논] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

더더욱.ex: 그 말을 들으니까 더더욱 가고 싶어졌어요.
더더욱.x: Hearing that made me want to go all the more.
더더욱.e: 더 'more' stacked on 더욱 'more': an extra-strong 'even more'.

상실하다.m: to lose (something important), to be deprived of
상실하다.x: He lost part of his memory in an accident.
상실하다.e: Two 'lose' syllables stacked — a serious, permanent loss.
상실하다.t: Used for abstract or serious losses like 기억, 자격, 의욕; for lost keys just say 잃어버리다.

굽히다.m: to bend; to give in, to yield
굽히다.ex: 그는 끝까지 자기 뜻을 굽히지 않았어요.
굽히다.x: He never backed down from his position.
굽히다.e: Causative of 굽다 'to be bent': literally 'make bent'.
굽히다.t: Pronounced [구피다] — ㅂ + ㅎ merges into ㅍ.

층간 소음.m: noise between floors (from upstairs or downstairs neighbors)
층간 소음.ex: 층간 소음 때문에 이웃과 자주 다퉈요.
층간 소음.x: We often argue with our neighbors because of noise between floors.
층간 소음.e: Literally 'between-floor noise': a top apartment complaint in Korea.
층간 소음.t: A big social issue in Korea; many people wear slippers or lay mats indoors to reduce it.

공론화.m: bringing an issue into public debate, making something a public issue
공론화.ex: 그 문제는 언론 보도를 통해 공론화되었어요.
공론화.x: That issue became a matter of public debate through media reports.
공론화.e: Literally 'becoming public discussion'; -화 = -ization: 공론화, 양극화, 세계화.
공론화.t: Pronounced [공논화] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.
rel: to bring up for public debate

납부.ex: 세금 납부 기한은 이번 달 말까지입니다.
납부.x: The deadline for paying taxes is the end of this month.
납부.t: Used for official payments like taxes and fees; for shopping, say 계산 or 결제.

중세.ex: 중세 유럽에서는 교회의 힘이 아주 강했어요.
중세.x: In medieval Europe, the church was very powerful.
중세.e: Literally 'middle age', just like the English.

녹조.ex: 여름마다 강에 녹조가 생겨서 문제가 돼요.
녹조.x: Every summer, algal blooms form in the river and cause problems.

묵인하다.m: to tacitly approve, to condone, to connive at
묵인하다.ex: 회사는 직원들의 초과 근무를 묵인해 왔어요.
묵인하다.x: The company has tacitly allowed its employees' overtime.

칭하다.m: to call, to name, to refer to as
칭하다.x: They called themselves guardians of the environment.
칭하다.t: Pattern: A을/를 B(이)라고 칭하다; 자칭 means 'self-proclaimed.'

헐뜯다.m: to speak ill of, to slander, to badmouth
헐뜯다.ex: 다른 사람을 뒤에서 헐뜯는 것은 좋지 않아요.
헐뜯다.x: It's not nice to badmouth people behind their backs.
헐뜯다.e: Probably 헐다 'to tear down' + 뜯다 'to tear off' — picking someone apart.

억척스럽다.ex: 어머니는 억척스럽게 일해서 우리 삼 남매를 키우셨어요.
억척스럽다.x: My mother worked tirelessly to raise us three kids.
억척스럽다.e: 억척 'tenacity' + -스럽다 'having that quality'; evokes the tough, hardworking mothers of postwar Korea.

파견직.ex: 파견직은 보통 정규직보다 고용이 훨씬 불안정한 편이에요.
파견직.x: Temp agency jobs are usually much less secure than regular positions.
파견직.e: Literally 'sent-out job' — hired by an agency, working elsewhere.

자유 무역.ex: 두 나라는 자유 무역 협정을 맺었습니다.
자유 무역.x: The two countries signed a free trade agreement.
자유 무역.e: Literally 'free trade'; FTA in Korean is 자유 무역 협정.

주주총회.m: shareholders' meeting, general meeting of shareholders
주주총회.ex: 다음 달에 정기 주주총회가 열릴 예정입니다.
주주총회.x: The annual shareholders' meeting will be held next month.
주주총회.t: Often shortened to 주총 in the news.

목판본.ex: 이 책은 조선 시대에 찍은 목판본이에요.
목판본.x: This book is a woodblock edition printed in the Joseon era.

문전성시.m: a crowd of visitors, being swamped with customers
문전성시.ex: 그 식당은 방송에 나온 뒤로 문전성시를 이루고 있어요.
문전성시.x: Since it was on TV, that restaurant has been packed with customers.
문전성시.e: Literally 'a market forms in front of the gate' — so many visitors.
문전성시.t: Common collocation: 문전성시를 이루다 'to be swamped with visitors'.

학벌주의.m: academic elitism, judging people by their school background
학벌주의.ex: 한국 사회의 학벌주의는 입시 경쟁을 더 심하게 만들어요.
학벌주의.x: Korean society's obsession with school pedigree makes entrance exam competition even fiercer.
학벌주의.e: 학벌 is one's school pedigree, i.e. which university one graduated from.

발전량.m: amount of power generated, power output
발전량.ex: 흐린 날에는 태양광 발전량이 크게 줄어들어요.
발전량.x: On cloudy days, solar power output drops sharply.
발전량.t: Pronounced [발쩐냥]: 전 becomes tense and ㄹ turns into ㄴ.

경국지색.m: a woman of breathtaking beauty, a femme fatale
경국지색.ex: 그녀는 옛 소설에 나오는 경국지색 같은 미인이었어요.
경국지색.x: She was a beauty like the country-toppling women of old novels.
경국지색.e: Literally 'beauty that topples a country', as a king neglects his rule.

신용경색.ex: 금융 위기 이후 심각한 신용경색이 나타났습니다.
신용경색.x: A severe credit crunch appeared after the financial crisis.
신용경색.e: Literally 'credit blockage': money stops flowing like a blocked blood vessel.
신용경색.t: Pronounced [시뇽경색]: the ㄴ links into 용.
